title: pernah — ever, once
pattern: Saya pernah … · Saya belum pernah … · Saya tidak pernah … · Pernah …? — Pernah. / Belum pernah.
explanation: pernah goes before a verb, or straight before ke for places, and says something has happened at least once: Saya pernah ke Lombok (I've been to Lombok). It's also how you ask 'have you ever': Pernah makan durian? (Have you ever had durian?). Answer with the word itself: Pernah (I have) or Belum pernah (not yet, I haven't). Tidak pernah is never, as a habit or a firm fact: Dia tidak pernah minum kopi (He never drinks coffee). With a situation in the past, pernah means once, at one time: Saya pernah tinggal di Jakarta (I lived in Jakarta at one point).
natural: Sudah pernah ke Bali? is one of the first questions a visitor gets, so have your answer ready. Belum pernah is the friendly reply for anything you might still do: Belum pernah, tapi saya mau coba.
stiff: Answer with pernah or belum pernah, not a bare ya or tidak; tidak on its own sounds like a flat 'no, never'. And tidak pernah in reply to an offer like Pernah coba sambal ini? can sound like you refuse to try it.

examples.english: Have you ever been to Lombok?

gap.why: 'Have you ever' is pernah; mau would ask whether he's going to Lombok.

examples.registerNotes: No verb is needed: pernah ke means 'have been to'. The answer is Pernah or Belum pernah.

examples.indonesian: Belum pernah, tapi saya mau coba.
examples.english: Not yet, but I'd like to try it.

gap.why: Belum pernah: not yet, and you'd like to. Tidak pernah would shut the door.

examples.registerNotes: A reply to Pernah makan durian? (Have you ever had durian?). Belum keeps it friendly: you just haven't had the chance.

gap.why: A firm habit is tidak pernah, never. Belum pernah would mean you haven't yet but might.

examples.registerNotes: Useful if you're vegetarian. At a warung, ask for the dish tanpa daging (without meat).

examples.indonesian: Waktu kecil, saya pernah tinggal di Jakarta.
examples.english: I lived in Jakarta for a while as a child.

gap.why: pernah marks something true at one time in the past; masih would mean you still live there.
